source: UserSim's store of Product Hunt users who were read in full (public profiles). Aggregates only: every group has 20 or more people; no names, ids or profile text.
accuracy: Group reactions are simulated. On 276 past launches they covered 65% [62, 67] of the broad points real commenters raised, but only about 9% of the exact issues - below a plain prompt with no personas (13.5%). Personas added nothing over real past comments (Nov 15, 19 launches), and group-specific behaviour inside a browser has not been validated.

groups.name: Product Evaluators
groups.who: These users have been on Product Hunt for a long time, have many followers, and are highly engaged with products, often providing detailed feedback and suggestions.
says: They provide detailed feedback on product functionality, user experience, and potential improvements.
They often compare new products to existing solutions or express concerns about pricing and trials.
They share personal anecdotes about how products impact their lives or work.
groups.votes_for: They upvote products related to Software Engineering, iOS, Sales, SaaS, and No-Code, often focusing on tools that enhance productivity and design.

groups.name: Product Makers
groups.who: These are highly active users who frequently comment and have launched multiple products, often identifying as founders, developers, or investors.
says: They introduce themselves as makers or founders, sharing their personal journey and inspiration behind their products.
They ask detailed questions about product functionality, ROI, and integration, often from a builder's perspective.
They express enthusiasm for privacy-focused tools and solutions that address common pain points in development or business.
groups.votes_for: They upvote products related to sales, SaaS, marketing, video, and open source, often with a focus on developer tools and APIs.

subgroups.name: Developer Marketers
subgroups.who: Highly engaged users with strong developer and marketer roles, high lifetime upvotes, and a significant number of followers, often linking to X and LinkedIn.
says: They introduce themselves as co-founders or engineers, offering technical insights and asking detailed questions about implementation.
They frequently congratulate teams on launches and express enthusiasm for new products.
They inquire about specific features, integrations, and technical specifications, often from a developer's perspective.
subgroups.votes_for: They show a strong interest in developer tools, APIs, open source projects, and products related to Mac, video, sales, and marketing.

subgroups.name: Design-Focused Founders
subgroups.who: Active users with prominent founder, product, designer, and marketer roles, moderate lifetime upvotes, and a good number of followers, often linking to LinkedIn.
says: They appreciate creativity and clever product positioning, often sharing personal anecdotes related to the product's problem space.
They express excitement for new features and improvements, sometimes from the perspective of a long-term user.
They ask practical questions about product functionality and potential use cases, especially for non-developers.
subgroups.votes_for: They are drawn to products in design tools, no-code solutions, Chrome extensions, sales, SaaS, education, and marketing.

subgroups.name: Emerging Dev Founders
subgroups.who: Newer users with strong developer and founder roles, lower lifetime upvotes, and fewer followers, often linking to LinkedIn.
says: They introduce themselves as solo developers or co-founders, sharing the personal inspiration and challenges behind their product.
They often describe their product as solving a specific personal pain point or a common industry problem.
They frequently use the 'Hey Product Hunt 👋 I'm [Name], and I built [Product]' format, emphasizing their direct involvement.
subgroups.votes_for: They are interested in tech, sales, social media, APIs, SaaS, developer tools, GitHub, and open source projects.

subgroups.name: Open Source Developers
subgroups.who: Highly technical users with strong developer and student roles, moderate lifetime upvotes, and a significant number of products launched, often linking to X, LinkedIn, and GitHub.
says: They provide detailed technical feedback and suggestions, often from a developer's perspective.
They share their own experiences building products, particularly those involving AI and developer tools.
They express enthusiasm for open-source projects and tools that simplify development workflows.
subgroups.votes_for: They prioritize open source, development, GitHub, developer tools, software engineering, APIs, Mac, and general tech products.

subgroups.name: Experienced SaaS Founders
subgroups.who: Very experienced users with high lifetime upvotes, many followers, and numerous products launched, often linking to X.
says: They share insights into the business and market aspects of products, including pricing strategies and scalability.
They often recount personal struggles or inefficiencies that a product aims to solve, particularly in sales, marketing, and data management.
They congratulate teams and express appreciation for well-executed products, sometimes highlighting specific team members.
subgroups.votes_for: They are interested in SaaS, marketing, social media, design tools, open source, no-code, video, and sales-related products.

groups.persona_brief: Founders and makers who ship their own launches: almost all have made or hunted a launch (92%) and nearly all comment (96%); founders, developers, investors and marketers are all over-represented (role lift 1.6-1.8x). They judge a product the way they judge their own: they read it as a builder, ask about ROI, integrations and how it works under the hood, and readily compare it to the SaaS, sales, marketing, video and open-source products they already use or have built. They respond well to privacy-minded tools that remove a common dev or business pain. They lose interest when the value or ROI is not clear quickly, when integration with their existing stack is unclear, or when it looks like a thin wrapper they could build themselves (inferred from their comment themes, not measured exits).

groups.name: Curious Observers
groups.who: This large group of users is relatively new to Product Hunt, has few upvotes or followers, and often lacks complete profile information, suggesting a more passive engagement.
says: They express curiosity about how products work and their core functionalities.
They often ask about specific features, platform compatibility (e.g., iOS release), or open-source availability.
They share initial impressions, often positive, and express interest in trying out new tools.
groups.votes_for: They upvote products across various categories including Vibe coding, Development, Social Media, Design Tools, and Productivity, showing a broad interest in new software.
groups.persona_brief: The largest group and the least invested: newer accounts with few upvotes or followers (median 1 upvote in the window), often no profile text; fewer founders and designers than average, relatively more students. Broad, casual interest across vibe coding, development, social media, design and productivity. They ask how the product works at a basic level, which features exist, platform availability (is there an iOS version?) and whether it is open source; first impressions are usually positive and they want to try it. They drop off when they cannot see what it does from the first screen, when sign-up or a paywall comes before any value, or when it is not on their platform (inferred from comment themes).

groups.name: Tech Innovators
groups.who: These users are highly engaged with a high number of upvotes, followers, and products launched, often identifying as developers, marketers, or product managers, and are keen on cutting-edge tech.
says: They discuss technical aspects of products, such as API usage, infrastructure, and integration capabilities.
They often inquire about pricing models, scalability, and how products differentiate from competitors.
They share personal experiences and use cases, often from a professional or technical standpoint.
groups.votes_for: They upvote products related to Mac, Developer Tools, GitHub, Tech, and Open Source, with a strong interest in innovative solutions and infrastructure.

subgroups.name: Product & Dev Launchers
subgroups.who: These users are highly active in launching products, often identifying as developers or product managers, and show strong engagement with developer tools and SaaS.
says: They frequently introduce their own products, explaining the problem they solve and their development journey.
They ask detailed technical questions about integrations, features, and underlying technologies.
They appreciate simplicity and lightweight solutions, often comparing new tools to existing ones.
subgroups.votes_for: They upvote products in Sales, SaaS, Social Media, Marketing, Video, and API categories, with a particular interest in Developer Tools.

subgroups.name: Connected Product Makers
subgroups.who: This segment consists of highly connected individuals, often founders, marketers, or developers, who are very active in commenting and launching products, with a strong online presence.
says: They frequently share their personal experiences and motivations behind building their products.
They engage in discussions about product design, user experience, and the practical application of new technologies.
They offer encouragement and congratulations to other makers, often highlighting specific features they appreciate.
subgroups.votes_for: They support launches in SaaS, No-Code, Design Tools, Education, Sales, and Marketing, showing a preference for products that enhance productivity and creativity.

subgroups.name: Tool Evaluators
subgroups.who: These users are relatively new to the platform, primarily upvoting rather than launching, and are interested in practical applications of new tools, often as product managers or marketers.
says: They frequently inquire about pricing, value proposition, and specific use cases to determine if a product is 'worth paying for'.
They ask about integrations and compatibility with existing workflows and platforms.
They express interest in how tools can simplify complex tasks and automate processes.
subgroups.votes_for: They favor products in Chrome Extensions, Design Tools, No-Code, Education, Social Media, and Productivity, focusing on tools that offer immediate utility.

subgroups.name: Mac & Dev Enthusiasts
subgroups.who: This segment is characterized by recent high activity, particularly in upvoting, and a strong interest in developer tools, open source, and Mac-specific applications, often identifying as developers or marketers.
says: They ask detailed questions about technical implementation, collaboration features, and scalability.
They share practical tips and creative uses for the products, often relating to personal productivity or workflow improvements.
They express a desire for Mac alternatives or specific platform support for new tools.
subgroups.votes_for: They are keen on products related to Mac, Developer Tools, GitHub, Open Source, and APIs, with a notable interest in software engineering solutions.

groups.persona_brief: The most active voters (median 20 upvotes in the window): developers, marketers and product managers (role lift 1.3-1.5x), leaning to Mac apps, developer tools, GitHub, APIs and infrastructure. They go straight to the technical details - API usage, infrastructure, integrations - and ask about pricing models, scalability and how the product differs from competitors they know. They relate it to their own work use case. They leave when pricing or scaling limits are vague, when it does not integrate with the tools they already run (Mac, GitHub, APIs), or when it looks like a me-too with no clear difference from an existing product (inferred from comment themes).

groups.name: Experienced Curators
groups.who: These are long-term, highly engaged users with significant lifetime upvotes and followers, who frequently comment and have launched products themselves.
says: They congratulate makers on launches and offer supportive feedback, often referencing prior knowledge of the product's development.
They share their own experiences and use cases for the products, highlighting practical benefits and suggesting improvements.
They discuss technical aspects like SDKs, APIs, and specific features, demonstrating a deep understanding of product development.
groups.votes_for: They support launches in iOS, software engineering, SaaS, sales, no-code, and design tools, showing interest in both technical and business-oriented solutions.

subgroups.name: Developer Founders
subgroups.who: These users are highly active founders and developers, often with design and marketing roles, who have launched multiple products and maintain a strong online presence.
says: They introduce their own products, detailing the problem they solved and the development journey.
They offer congratulations and specific feedback or questions about product features and functionality.
They share updates and express gratitude for support after their own product launches.
subgroups.votes_for: They upvote products in iOS, Sales, SaaS, No-Code, and Marketing, with a particular interest in Design Tools and general Tech.

subgroups.name: Mac & iOS Innovators
subgroups.who: This segment consists of long-term investors and founders with a significant number of followers and products launched, showing high engagement in commenting.
says: They introduce their own innovative products, often emphasizing local processing, open-source, or unique problem-solving.
They express enthusiasm and offer constructive feedback or questions about the technical aspects and potential of new tools.
They discuss the broader implications of new technologies, such as AI workflows and data privacy.
subgroups.votes_for: They show strong interest in iOS, Mac, Design Tools, Video, and SaaS, also engaging with Software Engineering, Marketing, and No-Code solutions.

subgroups.name: Software Engineering Founders
subgroups.who: These are experienced founders and product managers with a long history on the platform, high follower counts, and a strong tendency to launch products.
says: They introduce their own products, often focusing on solving specific workflow inefficiencies or creating bespoke software solutions.
They ask detailed questions about product functionality, integration, and performance, often comparing to existing solutions.
They provide positive feedback on design, onboarding, and the overall concept of new launches.
subgroups.votes_for: They are particularly interested in Software Engineering, SaaS, No-Code, and Sales, also showing engagement with Design Tools, Video, and Developer Tools.

main_groups_note: The 3 main clusters (E5). Prefer these; ids 0 (mostly inactive) and 6 (behaves like Product Makers) are kept for reference. 'What makes them leave' in the briefs is inferred from comment themes, not measured exits.
